reasons: Deviation call is correct: the original 15-day conformance window with an express cut-off of Vendor's correction/refund duty sits well below both the preferred (12 months software / 90 days services) and fallback (90/30) positions, and the cut-off sentence would neutralize the Section 19.4 remedy.

The redline reaches the preferred position directly: 12 months for Deliverables/software, 90 days for Services, and an affirmative statement that the Section 19.4 correction/replacement/refund obligations apply to nonconformities reported in the period — replacing rather than merely trimming the offending sentence.

The 0.681 changed-character ratio is justified here; the offending sentence both sets the period and extinguishes the remedy, so the clause had to be rewritten rather than word-patched. Other deterministic checks pass.

Comment is accurate, in-tone, cites the playbook position and offers the 90/30 fallback conditioned on the remedy surviving; it correctly describes both the period extension and the removal of the cut-off.

Minor drafting caution (not disqualifying): stating a 90-day period for the Section 19.1 Services warranty could be read as introducing a time limit where 19.1 previously had none; consider phrasing it as 'without limiting Section 19.1' if the services warranty is currently open-ended. Similarly, extending coverage to 'any software provided under this Agreement' broadens scope beyond the defined Deliverable, which is consistent with the playbook but should be confirmed against the software licensing terms.
